info.name: GraphQL Practice API

request.description: Every field the client can select on Query, with argument names and types. Note node/nodes and the deprecated authorById/postById.
Global object identification exposes the Node interface; possibleTypes are the entities that implement it.
authorById/postById report isDeprecated: true and the reason string.
Relay connection: totalCount, pageInfo and nodes. `first` is required (RequirePagingBoundaries = true). The GraphQL-Cost: report header returns the estimated cost in extensions.
Forward cursor pagination: pass the previous page's pageInfo.endCursor as `after`.
Backward pagination with `last` instead of `first`.
Filtering is passed as a typed `where` variable. Enum values are strings.
Boolean composition: `or`, `and`, `not`, plus string operators (contains, startsWith, eq, in).
Sorting is a list, so multiple keys are allowed (e.g. [{status: ASC}, {createdAt: DESC}]).
The three paging inputs composed; this is the shape the Blazor client sends.
Every connection gets its own generated filter input type (AuthorFilterInput, TagFilterInput, ...).

item.name: Post with author, tags and comment count

request.description: Author is a DataLoader (batched into one SQL query); tags/comments are nested connections. Watch the API console to see the single batched author query.
Deeply nested selection. Nested lists use [Parent(requires: nameof(T.Id))] so the join key is always projected.
QueryContext<T> pushes the selection into SQL: only the selected columns are queried (no SELECT *).
Copy the returned opaque ids into the collection variables postId/authorId/tagId. They are base64 of 'TypeName:localId' (e.g. QmxvZ1Bvc3Q6MQ== = BlogPost:1). The test script does this automatically.

item.name: Fetch any node by global id

request.description: One field fetches any entity. Inline fragments narrow to the concrete type. Change {{postId}} to {{authorId}} and swap the fragment to ... on Author to fetch an author instead.

item.name: Fetch many nodes by global id

request.description: Batch lookup. Mixed types come back as Node; each item resolves via its inline fragment. Requires the Node type name to match.
Passing a BlogPost id while selecting a Comment fragment: the fragment simply does not match, so only `id` is returned (no error).
authorById/postById still work (local int id) but are deprecated. Also note these fields return a nullable type, so id: 99999 yields null rather than an error.
Mutation conventions wrap arguments in a single `input` object. The test script stores the new author's global id in {{authorId}}.
authorId/tagIds are `[ID]` inputs, so they take global ids and Hot Chocolate decodes them to local keys. The test script stores blogPost.id in {{postId}} so Update/Delete below chain automatically.
Partial update: only the supplied fields change. Changing the title re-derives the slug. Uses {{postId}} captured by Create post.

exec: pm.test('{{postId}} is set (run Create post first)', () => pm.expect(pm.collectionVariables.get('postId'), 'postId').to.not.be.empty);

request.description: Returns the deleted post. Missing ids surface as a typed PostNotFoundError, not a GraphQL field error. Uses {{postId}}.
postId/authorId are global [ID] inputs. Also publishes to the dynamic topic OnCommentAdded_{postId} for subscribers. The test script stores the new comment's id in {{commentId}}.
Run twice: the second run reports the typed SlugAlreadyInUseError in the payload. The test script stores the new tag id in {{tagId}} on success.
deleteTag takes a global [ID] input. Uses {{tagId}}.
Errors because RequirePagingBoundaries = true: every connection needs first or last. Response is 200 with errors[].extensions.code = HC0082.
Schema validation failure: HTTP 400 with errors[].extensions.code = HC0012 (no path, since no execution happened).
Transport-level 400. Contrast with the 200 + errors[] responses above.
Returns extensions.cost with the estimated field/type cost instead of throwing. Cost multiplies across nested lists, so a large nested query can trip HC0047 (MaxFieldCost/MaxTypeCost = 10,000 here).
